data.command: Explain valid accounts as an initial access technique

data.text:
Valid accounts can be a sneaky way for attackers to get into a system. Essentially, an attacker finds a username and password that are still active and not changed by the system administrator.

One of the most common tools for finding valid accounts is called `nmap`. If I run `nmap -p- --host-timeout 10 <IP address>` (where `<IP address>` is the IP address of our server), it will scan the system for open ports. If a service is running on a particular port, the attacker might be able to connect to it using the valid account credentials.

For instance, if the ssh service is running on port 22, and the attacker knows the username and password, they can use a tool like `ssh` to connect to the server.

In Ubuntu 22.04.3 LTS, you can see the running services by using `systemctl status`. This will show you which services are currently active on the system. In this case, if the ssh service is running, you can see it by running `systemctl status ssh`.
